Elder Remains Here,
Calls At Kung's Home

Mr. James Elder, financial ad-
visor to Chang, Hsueh-liang and
whose arrival here last Friday has
aroused considerable speculation, is
still in Shanghai and is not ex-
pected to leave for the time being,
it was learned yesterday. ●
Mr. Elder left his room at the
Metropole Hotel on Monday morn-
ing and motored to the private re-
sidence of Dr. H. H. Kung, Vice-
President of the Executive Yuan
and Minister of Finance, at Rte.
Herve de Sieyes. The purpose of
his call was to inquire when Dr.
Kung would return to Shanghai
from Nanking.
Since his arrival, Mr. Elder has
been keeping his movements very
secret. He has also repeatedly re-
fused to give an interview to Chin-
ese newspaper reporters.

埃尔德仍留沪，
拜访孔祥熙寓所

据悉，张学良的财务顾问詹姆斯·埃尔德（James Elder）先生上周五抵沪后引发了诸多猜测，但他目前仍留在上海，且暂时预计不会离开。●
埃尔德先生于周一上午离开其在大都会酒店（Metropole Hotel）的房间，乘车前往行政院副院长兼财政部长孔祥熙博士位于西爱咸斯路（Rte. Herve de Sieyes）的私宅。他此次拜访的目的是询问孔博士何时从南京返回上海。
自抵沪以来，埃尔德先生一直对其行踪严加保密。他也多次拒绝接受中国报纸记者的采访。

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, DECEMBER 20, 1936 18018
7166

Elder Avoids Reporters,
Pleads “I Know Nothing”

Genially parrying off questions asking him to reconstruct the events immediately before and after the Sian revolt, Mr. James Elder, close friend of Chang Hsueh-liang and the first man to arrive in Shanghai since the outbreak of the trouble, refused yesterday to be interviewed on any aspects of the coup engineered by the “Young Marshal.”

Willing to talk to the reporter on any other topic, Mr. Elder preferred yesterday to limit his statement on the Sian situation to “I know nothing.”

He was in the Shensi capital when the revolt broke out, he said, but he did not gather all the information on the trouble until he arrived in Nanking and Shanghai. Sian, he explained, is a big city, and when the coup took place, he was some 30 miles away from the storm center. His only knowledge of the revolt he said, was a number of rifle reports he heard.

Arriving here Friday night by train from Nanking, Mr. Elder made every effort to evade a group of newsmen who greeted him at the station. Yesterday he was sought after by a number of correspondents and reporters to give an account of the coup.

To these newspapermen, Mr. Elder gave the same answer, claiming that he knows nothing about the situation. He added that he went to Nanking to tender his personal sympathy to Madame Chiang Kai-shek.

Denying any connection with the “Peace negotiation,” Mr. Elder told newsmen that he is not authorized, asked or deputed to act as a go-between.

Stocky, well-groomed, Mr. Elder is known here as a close associate of the “Young Marshal,” with whom he worked and played during the years they spent in Mukden and Peiping. Mr. Elder denied yesterday that he holds an official position as the “financial adviser” to the Chang.

His aversion of the public limelight was shown yesterday when asked to pose for a picture. “It’s just a waste of time. I never like to have my pictures taken,” he told a press photographer.

《字林西报》，1936年12月20日，星期日 18018
7166

埃尔德回避记者，
声称“我一无所知”

詹姆斯·埃尔德先生是张学良的密友，也是事变爆发后首位抵达上海的人士。昨日，他婉拒了就“少帅”策划的政变任何方面接受采访，并和蔼地回避了要求他重构西安事变前后经过的提问。

埃尔德先生愿意就任何其他话题与记者交谈，但昨日他倾向于将关于西安局势的声明限制为“我一无所知”。

他说，事变爆发时他身在陕西省会，但直到抵达南京和上海后，他才收集到有关事变的全面信息。他解释说，西安是一座大城市，政变发生时，他距离风暴中心约30英里。他说，他对叛乱的唯一了解就是听到几声枪响。

埃尔德先生周五晚乘火车从南京抵沪，竭尽全力躲避在车站迎接他的一群新闻界人士。昨日，许多通讯员和记者追访他，要求他叙述政变经过。

对这些报界人士，埃尔德先生给出了同样的回答，声称他对局势一无所知。他补充说，他去南京是为了向蒋介石夫人表达个人的慰问。

埃尔德先生否认与“和平谈判”有任何关联，他告诉新闻界人士，他未获授权、未被请求或被委派担任中间人。

埃尔德先生身材矮壮，衣着整洁，在此间被视为“少帅”的亲密伙伴，两人在沈阳和北平度过的岁月里曾共事并一同娱乐。埃尔德先生昨日否认自己担任张氏的“财务顾问”这一正式职位。

昨日当被要求拍照时，他表现出了对公众关注的厌恶。“这简直是浪费时间。我从不喜欢让人给我拍照，”他对一位新闻摄影记者说道。

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, DECEMBER 19, 1936
18031

Elder, Financial Adviser To Revolt Chief, Thought Here

Mr. James Elder, financial adviser reported to have received strict instructions from his employer not to talk, especially to strangers, made the task of finding him among the passengers of the Nanking train difficult.

**Train Late**
The Nanking train, delayed by the derailment earlier in the day, was late. Before the train arrived a group of five reporters and correspondents scattered themselves at different vantage points along the platform to make sure that they would not miss the incoming passenger whom they were interested to meet.

When the express steamed into the station, attention of the newsmen was collectively centered on the first-class coaches in which they believed Mr. Elder would be located.

Before the train came completely to a stop a foreigner, carrying a light bag and wearing a dark coat and a cap, jumped off from one of the second-class coaches. His appearance convinced the correspondents that he was Mr. Elder. As the mysterious passenger hurriedly shouldered his way out of the crowd, one newshawk managed to follow him.

Outside the railing which led to the station foyer, the man believed to be the adviser, was met by another foreigner and a Chinese. They each took a ricksha, although it is known that a car had been sent to meet them.

With the reporter trailing behind, the man headed toward the downtown section. He was seen to take a cab at the Jinkee Road Station of the Ford Hire Service.

Mr. Elder was the foreigner who started for Nanking in a Eurasia plane from Loyang. The ship was forced down by bad weather at Penapu in Southern Anhwei. He continued by train and arrived in Nanking late that night. In the Capital, he had been closely guarded from pressmen and in conference with Government officials.

The financial adviser was first believed to be Mr. W. H. Donald, when his plane was forced down on its way to Nanking. This led to the report at one time that the Australian adviser of Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek was returning to the Capital instead of going back to Sian as originally planned.

The visit of Mr. Elder to Nanking was interpreted here as indicative of the willingness of the "Young Marshal" to retrace his steps and to liquidate the Sian revolt.

Mr. James Elder, financial adviser to Chang Hsueh-liang, is believed to have arrived here shortly before 12 o'clock last night on the Nanking train.

Although he denied his identity when questioned, newspapermen who recognize the American adviser by sight were positive that a man who hurried off from the station as soon as the train arrived was Mr. Elder.

Mr. Elder, according to reports reaching here yesterday from Nanking, had arrived in the capital from Sian and was proceeding to this city by the afternoon train.

This report brought a group of newsmen to the North Station in an effort to locate and to interview him.

据信叛乱首领的财务顾问埃尔德抵沪

据报道，詹姆斯·埃尔德先生作为财务顾问，已收到雇主的严格指示不得交谈，尤其是不得与陌生人交谈，这使得在南京列车的乘客中寻找他的任务变得困难。

**列车晚点**
南京列车因当天早些时候发生的脱轨事故而延误。在列车到达之前，五名记者和通讯员分散在站台的不同有利位置，以确保不会错过他们希望见到的 incoming 乘客。

当特快列车驶入车站时，记者们的注意力集体集中在他们认为埃尔德先生所在的一等车厢上。

在列车完全停稳之前，一名外国人提着一个轻便手提包，身穿深色大衣，头戴帽子，从其中一节二等车厢跳下。他的外貌使通讯员们确信他就是埃尔德先生。当这位神秘的乘客匆忙挤过人群时，一名新闻记者设法跟上了他。

在通往车站门厅的栏杆外，这名被认为是顾问的男子遇到了另一名外国人和一名中国人。尽管已知有一辆汽车派来接他们，但他们各自乘坐了一辆人力车。

在记者的尾随下，该男子朝市中心方向走去。有人看到他在福特租车服务处（Ford Hire Service）的金基路站（Jinkee Road Station）叫了一辆出租车。

埃尔德先生是那名从洛阳乘坐欧亚航空公司飞机前往南京的外国人。该飞机因恶劣天气被迫降落在皖南的彭埠（Penapu）。他继续乘火车前行，并于当晚深夜抵达南京。在首都，他被严密保护以免受记者打扰，并与政府官员进行了会谈。

起初，当他的飞机在前往南京途中被迫降落时，人们认为这位财务顾问是W. H. 唐纳德（W. H. Donald）先生。这导致一度有报道称，蒋介石总司令的澳大利亚顾问正返回首都，而不是按原计划返回西安。

埃尔德先生访问南京在此间被解读为表明“少帅”愿意回头并平息西安事变。

据信，张学良的财务顾问詹姆斯·埃尔德先生于昨晚12点前不久乘南京列车抵沪。

尽管在接受询问时他否认了自己的身份，但那些凭面貌认出这位美国顾问的新闻记者肯定，列车一到站就匆匆离开车站的那个人就是埃尔德先生。

根据昨日从南京传至此间的报道，埃尔德先生已从西安抵达首都，并将乘下午的列车前来本市。

这一消息引来一群新闻记者前往北站，试图找到并采访他。

SIN HAN PHO
Activities of Mr. J. Elder
Mr. James Elder, economic advisor to General
Chang Hsueh Liang, arrived in Nanking on December 18 acting
on instructions from the young Marshal. On th evening
of that day, he came to Shanghai and sojourned at the
Metropole Hotel, Kiangse Road.
On the morning of December 19, Mr. Elder
was very busy in approaching the various sources interested.
He will return to Nanking to-day whence he will proceed to
Sian to call on General Chang Hsueh Liang.

《新汉报》
J. 埃尔德先生的活动
张学良将军的经济顾问詹姆斯·埃尔德先生于12月18日奉少帅之命抵达南京。当晚，他来到上海，寄住在江西路的大都会酒店。
12月19日上午，埃尔德先生忙于接触各方相关人士。他将于今日返回南京，随后前往西安拜会张学良将军。

REPORT
Date December 9, 1936.

Subject James C. ELDER, Personal Adviser to Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang.

Made by D. S. Pitts. Forwarded by J. Boyne D.S.I

James C. ELDER, British, aged 33, returned to China from the United Kingdom via Genoa on September 10, 1936 as a passenger on board the s.s. "Scharnhorst." He was accompanied by Mrs. Elder, who is Russian by birth, and who is regarded in well-to-do circles as a lady in the strictest meaning of the word.

After arrival in Shanghai Mrs. & Mr. Elder, who is Personal Adviser to Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang, having been employed in this capacity for a number of years, stayed at the Metropole Hotel for two days, after which they returned to Hankow where they are permanently domiciled.

They both returned to Shanghai on October 29, 1936 and stayed at the Metropole Hotel for a few days before going back to Hankow. On November 20, 1936 Mr. Elder again returned to Shanghai, when he entered the Country Hospital as a patient of Dr. Joseph Preuss, 882 Bubbling Well Road, suffering from chronic dysentery. After treatment he left this hospital on November 29 and returned to his home in Hankow.

Enquiries show that Mr. Elder's private life will bear the closest inspection and there is not the slightest indication that he has ever been connected with activities of an unsavoury nature.

（印：SPECIAL BRANCH SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE 10 DEC. 1936）

Ja. Pitts.
D. S.

D.C. (Special Branch).

报告
日期：1936年12月9日。

主题：詹姆斯·C·埃尔德（James C. ELDER），张学良元帅的个人顾问。

制作人：D. S. 皮茨（D. S. Pitts）。转呈人：J. 博伊恩（J. Boyne），副巡官（D.S.I）

詹姆斯·C·埃尔德，英国人，33岁，于1936年9月10日作为乘客乘坐“沙恩霍斯特”号（s.s. "Scharnhorst"）轮船，经热那亚从英国返回中国。陪同他的是埃尔德夫人，她出生于俄罗斯，在富裕阶层中被视为一位名副其实的淑女。

埃尔德夫妇抵沪后，身为张学良元帅个人顾问（已在此职位任职多年）的埃尔德先生在大都会酒店住了两天，随后返回他们永久定居地汉口。

两人于1936年10月29日再次回到上海，在大都会酒店停留数日后返回汉口。1936年11月20日，埃尔德先生再次回到上海，因患慢性痢疾，作为约瑟夫·普鲁斯（Joseph Preuss）医生（地址：静安寺路882号）的病人入住宏恩医院（Country Hospital）。治疗后，他于11月29日出院，返回汉口的家中。

调查显示，埃尔德先生的私人生活经得起最严格的审查，没有任何迹象表明他曾参与任何不名誉的活动。

（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处特别处 1936年12月10日）
